data.deltaContent: I
've been overlooking the key relationship here:
`self@` actually refers to `self.upool@`, not `phys_view().frames`. This means the manager's view is fundamentally the
UserPool's view. When the kernel calls `frame::alloc()` as a free function without any self reference
, it doesn't modify `self.upool`, so that invariant stays intact across the allocation.
But
now I'm hitting a logical contradiction. The wrapper `alloc_kernel_frame` needs to satisfy
`self@ == old(self)@.alloc_one(kf@)`, yet since `self@` equals `self
.upool@` and the kernel alloc doesn't touch the upool, `self@` literally doesn't change—meaning
`self@ == old(self)@`. That makes the postcondition `self@ == old(self)@.alloc_one(kf
@)` impossible to satisfy, since it would require `old(self)@ == old(self)@.alloc_one(addr)`, which is false. The
`lemma_kernel_alloc_one` admit tries to bridge this gap, but it's asserting something structurally contrad

ictory.
